Quantum Upgrade Could Be 'Particularly Challenging' for Blockchains: IOSCO

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (807 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.
  • Sources indicate that A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) said in a report published on Thursday.
  • "Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais noted in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.

Sources indicate that A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) said in a report published on Thursday. The cyber readiness challenge posed by quantum computing "is immediate and requires action," it said.

"Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais noted in a statement.

The 63-page report cited conservative estimates that such machines could emerge between 2030 and 2035. Several industry participants consulted by IOSCO went further, arguing that firms should prepare for the possibility that they arrive within five years, potentially accelerated by AI.

IOSCO mentioned the migration may be particularly challenging for blockchains, because cryptography is embedded in their core architecture and any change requires coordinated action across decentralized networks. Public blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana and Tron rely heavily on elliptic curve cryptography to verify identities and validate transactions, and a powerful enough quantum computer could derive private keys from exposed public keys, a scenario known as "Q-Day.".

According to recent reports, swapping in quantum-resistant signatures comes at a cost. Signatures under ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, are about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than today's 64-byte elliptic curve signatures, the report said. It cited evidence from a quantum-resistant Solana testnet that saw throughput fall by about 90% when post-quantum signatures replaced existing ones.

Sources indicate that because the cryptography sits in transaction formats and consensus rules, replacing it requires hard forks, and decentralized networks have no way to force quick adoption, making migration "slow and fragmented," IOSCO remarked. Accounts and smart contracts still controlled by vulnerable keys could stay exposed after a network adds quantum-resistant options, and the path to quantum resistance for Bitcoin wallets remains uphill.

Industry observers note that wallet makers face their own trade-offs. SHRINCS, the leading candidate for a post-quantum Bitcoin signature scheme, offers "stateful" signatures that are about 10 times smaller but can expose funds to theft if keys are reused beyond a set signing budget, Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka has remarked. Trezor is considering making the larger, safer stateless option the default, and hardware wallets will also need post-quantum cryptography for firmware and device authentication, he added.

The report distinguished "on-spend" attacks, in which an attacker races to exploit a public key revealed by a pending transaction, from "at-rest" attacks on keys left exposed for longer. Dormant or abandoned coins pose a particular problem where their holders can't move them. Crypto firms have formed a quantum alliance as some 6 million BTC sit in exposed addresses, and Bitcoin developer Cory Fields has proposed "quantum landmines" to make attacks on such coins costly.

Layer-2 networks are not insulated either. Optimistic rollups could face forged signatures during their dispute windows, typically seven days on Ethereum, and many zero-knowledge rollups use SNARK proofs that rely on elliptic curves. Hash-based STARK proofs are more resistant, but a rollup is only as safe as the layer-1 contracts, bridges and governance keys it depends on, the report said.

Developers are already working on fixes. Researchers have proposed several ways to make Bitcoin quantum-safe, StarkWare has shown a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction, and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has noted the network is betting its future on quantum resistance.

It has been revealed that IOSCO said firms should migrate to post-quantum cryptography and build "crypto-agility," the ability to patch cryptographic systems without major redesign. Quantum key distribution could complement those measures on selected high-security channels, it added.

Sources indicate that most preparations across financial markets are still at an early stage, focused on awareness, governance, training and identifying vulnerable systems, according to the report, which drew on a March 2026 survey of members of IOSCO's Fintech Task Force and discussions with experts. Some respondents described "quantum-procrastination," in which firms put off action while waiting for clearer regulatory signals or wider adoption.

No surveyed jurisdiction reported operational deployment of quantum computing in regulated financial services. The watchdog also urged regulators to act against "quantum washing," in which firms overstate the role, maturity or performance of quantum technology. IOSCO said it will treat quantum as a priority in 2027, focusing on raising awareness across the financial ecosystem.

Quantum hardware is advancing swiftly. IBM has claimed a trusted quantum advantage, and Google has mentioned it has cracked some of the field's biggest bottlenecks.

Industry observers note that NEAR Protocol (NEAR) fell 11.41% on Nov. 20 and traded at $2.84, according to TradingView data. In early October, the token was trading near $6, and it has lost about half of its value since then.

Industry observers note that over the same period, the volume of NEAR Intents went up. "NEAR went from $6 to $3 in about a month. funny thing is, NEAR Intents is doing more volume now than it did in october," NEAR ecosystem contributor Evgeny Haenko wrote on X on Nov. 20.

Sources indicate that according to Haenko, NEAR Intents averaged around $129 million in daily volume in October, and in November it was processing around $134 million a day. "The price got cut in half, the business didn't slow down at all. hard for me to be bearish here," he wrote.

NEAR Intents lets people swap assets across more than 30 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP. The service is built into wallets such as Ledger, Trust Wallet and Brave. Over the past year, its trading volume grew 7.1 times to $39.5 billion.

In a recent development, NEAR Intents has collected about $63 million in fees in total, and the network keeps about 29% of that amount. Fees on the NEAR Intents interface, payments from B2B partners and the spread on better-than-market trades accounted for 16.3%, 9.9% and 2.8% of the fees, respectively. Over the last 30 days, the protocol earned about $1.8 million, compared with $2.2 million in October.

In a recent development, since February 2026, the protocol has used NEAR Intents revenue to buy NEAR on the market. More than 1.84 million NEAR have gone to the buyback wallet so far, and that is 41.6% of all distributed onchain revenue. Base transaction fees on the network are burned in full.

In early November, the NEAR community also voted to cut the maximum annual issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over two years. The proposal, HSP-029, went through House of Stake, NEAR's governance initiative, and Haenko is one of its participants.

On Sept. 29, Bitwise debuted the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF on NYSE Arca under the ticker NRR. Two days later, on Oct. 1, NEAR Intents paused its services after an exploit that cost about $3.8 million, and the team promised to compensate consumers in full. The exploiter later returned the funds. "The funds from the $3.8M NEAR Intents hack were sent back in full," NEAR Intents general manager Alex Shevchenko said at the time.

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia.

Tokenized Take-Two shares saw a massive 24-hour trading spike as on-chain markets attract Washington scrutiny.

The long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI didn’t just break gaming records—it briefly turned publisher Take-Two Interactive into the hottest stock on the blockchain, outselling even AI giant Nvidia.

On November 18, decentralized exchange (DEX) trading volume for tokenized Take-Two shares (TTWO) exploded by 578%, jumping from $36.8 million to $249.5 million in a single day, according to Token Terminal data.

That was roughly 2.8 times the $88.1 million traded in tokenized Nvidia (NVDA) shares over the same 24-hour window, accounting for 42% of all on-chain stock trading.

Nearly all of the action, roughly $239 million, or 96% of total volume, happened on Solana via Backpack Securities, a subsidiary of crypto exchange Backpack. Rolled out earlier this year, the token is designed to be backed 1:1 by real Take-Two shares held in custody.

Traditional Wall Street traders saw a much calmer reaction: Take-Two’s Nasdaq shares rose 6.2% to close at $216.61 on launch day before pulling back 3.7% to $208.65 the next session.

Despite Take-Two’s one-day viral spike, Nvidia remains the undisputed heavyweight of tokenized equities, boasting a $399.4 million market cap and $2 billion in 30-day trading volume (compared to Take-Two’s $808.1 million).

Overall, tokenized public stocks on Solana have nearly doubled since late October to reach $1.22 billion.

Sources indicate that that rapid growth is drawing fresh scrutiny in Washington. On November 16, four Democratic senators sent a letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) questioning how its newly introduced exemption for tokenized securities would address investor protection and anti-money laundering requirements.

It has been revealed that the problem also surfaced during the November 19 Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing for Kristin Johnson, President Donald Trump’s nominee for the SEC. Johnson indicated that exemptions covering tokenized stocks should eventually be formalized through rules following a public comment period.

The TTWO spike highlights tokenized stocks can attract event-driven trading on-chain, comparable to some of the largest names in the segment. It also coincides with growing regulatory scrutiny of how tokenized stocks are supervised.

  • The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that things have changed dramatically since the third quarter of 2026, when institutional interest in Bitcoin [BTC] increased. After three quarters of net selling, institutional investors resumed net purchases of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products (ETPs).

In a recent development, according to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period. Notably, by the 30th of September, institutional investment managers held a record 356,491 BTC-equivalent, worth approximately $29.78 billion.

The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.

Together, they held 144,307 BTC-equivalent by the end of September, representing 40.5% of all Bitcoin ETP holdings reported by institutional managers. If looked back, their holdings have increased for nine consecutive quarters and are now 3.3 times higher than their March 2024 levels.

That being remarked, large banks played a major role in this accumulation, with Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley being among the biggest buyers during Q3.

It has been revealed that wells Fargo alone added 14,636 BTC-equivalent, taking its total holdings to 30,553 BTC-equivalent, making it the largest institutional holder of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs, overtaking Jane Street.

Institutional ownership also shifted, with hedge funds dropping from 50.6% in December 2024 to 19%, while financial advisors and wealth platforms increased their exposure. Of this, BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for 65.2% of institutional Bitcoin ETP holdings.

That remarked, Bitcoin ETP holdings fell by 38,531 BTC between the 30th of September and the 16th of November.

However, the tokenized ETP sector continued to struggle, with its market capitalization falling 6.2% to $595 million and trading volume declining to $160 million, as previously reported by AMBCrypto.

In a recent development, this comes as Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded net inflows of $2.65 billion in September 2026 and $3.52 billion in August, while July saw smaller inflows of $172.43 million. However, the trend reversed in October, with $515.03 million in net outflows, followed by significantly larger outflows of $3.47 billion in November 2026.

  • Charles Hoskinson’s Cardano-linked privacy blockchain Midnight has inked a significant initial deal with a Japanese payments firm as it aims to make further inroads into traditional finance.
  • The news comes soon after a key breakthrough for Midnight in the United Kingdom, where Monument Bank started tokenizing customer deposits on the blockchain.
  • 19 NADA NEWS report, Midnight Foundation President Fahmi Syed stated the foundation had inked an MOU (memorandum of understanding) with a major Japanese payments organization.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charles Hoskinson’s Cardano-linked privacy blockchain Midnight has inked a significant initial deal with a Japanese payments firm as it aims to make further inroads into traditional finance.

The news comes soon after a key breakthrough for Midnight in the United Kingdom, where Monument Bank started tokenizing customer deposits on the blockchain.

Sources indicate that per a Nov. 19 NADA NEWS report, Midnight Foundation President Fahmi Syed stated the foundation had inked an MOU (memorandum of understanding) with a major Japanese payments organization.

Syed did not name the organization. But the deal is a major one for Midnight’s bid to establish a presence in Japan’s financial services sector.

However, it is just an initial agreement, and no commercial services have been rolled out in Japan yet.

It is also worth noting that the Midnight Foundation is talking to some major Japanese banks and companies working with intellectual property and medical data.

According to Syed, he spent two days in Tokyo meeting with major financial institutions and other companies.

Japan has been a key market for Midnight, along with the United States.

According to Midnight Foundation Japan country manager Taro Kimura, Japan is the only Asian country where the foundation has a local representative on the ground.

Midnight has been eyeing Japan more keenly due to the country’s sizeable Cardano community.

The Japanese push comes hot on the heels of a historic development in the British banking sector.

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 18, British financial institution Monument Bank started tokenizing retail customer deposits on Midnight. It is the first UK bank to launch such a product on a public blockchain.

Sources indicate that the first phase of the venture involves up to £250 million in tokenized deposits. For this, the bank is offering customers a 12-month fixed annual interest rate of 5.2%.

Midnight employs zero-knowledge cryptography to safeguard sensitive transaction details, unlike traditional public blockchains. As a result, banks can meet compliance requirements while keeping their customers’ private information and transaction details out of public view.

Home » Altcoins » Dozens of Seats Go Unclaimed At Donald Trump’s Memecoin Dinner.

Presently, only 130 crypto whale wallets qualified for Trump’s fancy memecoin dinner at the golf club.

In a recent development, just 130 crypto wallets secured seats for the November 22 TRUMP token holder dinner at Donald Trump’s Virginia golf club, leaving dozens of the 185 available places unclaimed. The Official Trump token was trading near record lows at the time of the close.

Industry observers note that the event is designed to reward the largest holders, with the top 29 wallets also eligible for a VIP reception. Contest participants held roughly $8.6 million in tokens combined when the qualification period ended, a sharp drop in engagement from the project’s first holder dinner.

It has been revealed that BREAKING: 🇺🇸 Trump will host an exclusive dinner for the top 185 $TRUMP holders this Sunday.The coin is down 99% from its peak. pic.twitter.com/NxizWHlrVg.

Ranking was based on time-weighted holdings, which encouraged accumulation and retention through the window.

It has been revealed that more than 5,000 eligible holders reportedly did not register. The leaderboard’s combined value represented only a small fraction of TRUMP’s roughly $268 million market capitalization.

In a recent development, TRUMP was trading around $0.95 in the latest reporting, down roughly 46% over the prior month after setting a record low near $0.896 on November 14. The token remains well below its peak, with one account describing it as down almost 99% from its high.

Large holders added to positions during the dip. Nansen data showed the top 100 wallets increased their combined holdings by 1.27% over 30 days, while a separate whale cohort expanded holdings by 26.63%. Exchange balances fell slightly over the same period.

Holding incentives are temporary.

Top-ranked winners risk losing VIP benefits if balances drop below specified levels before the event, and lower-ranked winners can forfeit their seat by selling more than half their qualifying balance. Those restrictions expire once the dinner is over.

Ahead of the 2025 dinner, 92 of 220 invited holders reportedly sold their entire positions before the event.

A Super Bowl-themed leaderboard planned for February 2027 may give some buyers a reason to stay involved, but it does not remove the immediate question of whether winners will take liquidity afterward.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that vanEck has terminated Gemini as custodian and clearing agent for three U.S.
  • As per three 8-K filings from the 19th of November, VanEck Digital Assets delivered written termination notices to Gemini Trust Tech giant on the 16th of November, with the contract set to officially end on 16th February.
  • The notice ended custody and clearing arrangements for the VanEck Bitcoin ETF (HODL) and the VanEck Ethereum ETF (ETHV).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that vanEck has terminated Gemini as custodian and clearing agent for three U.S. crypto ETFs. In doing so, it has made Coinbase Custody its sole remaining safekeeper, thus putting into jeopardy the Solana fund’s staking future.

As per three 8-K filings from the 19th of November, VanEck Digital Assets delivered written termination notices to Gemini Trust Tech giant on the 16th of November, with the contract set to officially end on 16th February.

The notice ended custody and clearing arrangements for the VanEck Bitcoin ETF (HODL) and the VanEck Ethereum ETF (ETHV).

The third ETF, the VanEck Solana ETF (VSOL), is the most affected one in this regard, because there is no news on who will take over staking services for it. Market participants are assuming it is Coinbase, but as of now, there is no confirmation yet.

According to recent reports, as expected, the filings have opened a series of questions, as they have not established the allocation of assets between Gemini and Coinbase. This, in turn, has made it impossible to quantify precisely what Gemini is losing in dollar terms.

The filing also failed to explain why VanEck chose to terminate the agreements now, with roughly three months of notice before the effective date. Moreover, they did not even address the staking question that matters most for VSOL shareholders.

According to recent reports, this comes as the crypto ETF landscape has been in a consolidation for a while now, with Coinbase already being a custodian for most U.S. Spot crypto ETFs.

All in all, VanEck’s current decision to put an end to its Gemini arrangements has left it with a single custodian across all three funds and a massive unresolved operational gap.

What’s left now is that by 16th February, 2027, the firm will have to find a upcoming staking provider for VSOL.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less than half of all Bitcoin [BTC] is green right now, and that’s not a good look. In fact, as it turns out, we may not see light anytime soon.

As of 18th November, those are the numbers. At least according to the Rand Group.

It has been revealed that every major BTC bottom since 2015 has happened with less than half the supply in the green. In August 2025, that figure was 35.7%. It hit 39.8% in December 2018, 42.5% in March 2020, and 44.8% in November 2022.

This June, it was as low as 46.9%.

Each low has come in a little higher than the one before. Holders are giving up less ground with every cycle. The argument is that the best opportunities show up when most holders are underwater, not when everyone’s celebrating.

Industry observers note that hence, the question: Does that mean the bottom is in? No, But Bitcoin is in a zone where that has mattered before.

… might be tech stocks and rates, according to QCP Capital.

Not everyone’s ready to call it a bottom, yet. In fact, the digital asset partner thinks Bitcoin’s problem is about money getting tight everywhere.

It has been revealed that earlier this cycle, ETF buying, corporate treasuries, and hopes of rate cuts did a good job of soaking up selling. That support will crack when stocks drop across the board.

So, what would it take to turn things around?

Its report cited three things, namely,.

…recovery will likely require stabilisation in technology equities, reduced volatility in rates and evidence that institutional flows are returning.

Recent findings suggest that until then, any bounce driven by shorts closing out could fizzle fast. The Fed could also be another weight on BTC’s back.

Recent findings suggest that at the time of writing, the charts weren’t really comforting either. BTC was trading at $58,681, down 5.2% over the last 24 hours. Just a couple of weeks ago, it was trading above $80K.

In a recent development, the RSI was knee deep in oversold territory, its lowest reading in months. Sellers have been running out fuel, but oversold conditions can stay as such for a while.

Sources indicate that the ADX was 43.8 and still rising. So, the downtrend seemed to be getting stronger. Especially since buyers didn’t look like they were going to turn up.

Recent findings suggest that this is a bottom range that we know. However, until the selling pressure slows down, calling it the floor would be a gamble.

What to Wear to Thanksgiving: 6 Outfit Ideas for Every Type of Gathering

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that with Thanksgiving just around the corner, I’ve already started thinking about two very important things: what’s going on the dinner table and what I’ll wear.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Recent findings suggest that with Thanksgiving just around the corner, I’ve already started thinking about two very important things: what’s going on the dinner table and what I’ll wear. I’m especially looking forward to my mom’s baked mashed potatoes (a family favorite) and the homemade mac and cheese I’ll be bringing along. But, especially as a style writer, half the fun of the holidays is having a good excuse to put together a good outfit.

My family’s Thanksgiving gatherings tend to be pretty casual, so I’m not one to show up in anything overly dressy or uncomfortable. I’m usually somewhere in the middle, opting for an outfit that looks like I made an effort but still lets me enjoy a second helping of stuffing without worrying about a too-tight waistband. Think a great sweater with loose-fitting jeans, a knit dress with boots, or even a smartly-styled leggings outfit. Because as much as I love dressing up for the holidays, I also want to enjoy post-dinner card games or sit comfortably on the couch afterward.

If you’re approaching Thanksgiving dressing the same way, I’ve rounded up six outfit ideas to help get you inspired. I’ve included a few options perfect for a Christmas card photoshoot, along with more laid-back looks that are just as fitting for a casual family gathering. No matter what your holiday intends look like, these outfits strike that happy medium between looking good and feeling comfortable. Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have some mac and cheese to make.

According to recent reports, in my opinion, there’s no outfit more perfect for the holidays than a sweater dress and boots. It’s cute enough for family photos but loose and soft enough to keep you comfy all day (especially if you kick the boots off at the door). Grab a long-sleeve knit dress that hits somewhere between mid-thigh and the knee and pair it with some fleece-lined tights and your fave knee-high boot. A midi or maxi dress with an ankle bootie works too.

Express Mock Neck Mini Sweater Dress.

Sam Edelman Sylvia Knee-High Boot.

Start by pulling out a denim jacket and denim skirt. From there, add a plain white T-shirt. I love brown for the fall, so I wore my version of this outfit with brown boots and a matching brown belt and bag. I love this combo because it looks super stylish, but I don’t feel overdressed or uncomfortable when I wear it. Don’t have a denim skirt or jacket? No problem. You can recreate this look with a leather jacket, jeans, or any neutral mini skirt.

Presics Supima Cotton Box Cut T-Shirt.

Start with a pair of satin or silk pants and pair them with a sweater and ballet flats in the same shade. This outfit has been one of my go-tos lately because it’s so comfortable, but the monochrome palette and shiny finish of the pants make it look like I tried way harder than I actually did. You can even make it feel a little dressier by swapping the flats for a pair of pointed-toe ankle boots.

It doesn’t get comfier than leggings and slippers. For ultra-casual gatherings when you just want to focus on family and food without looking frumpy, just style yours a little smarter. Go for a pair of leggings with minimal seaming (especially a pair without a front seam), which makes them look sleeker. Then grab a dressy-looking oversized sweater—something with a boxy cut, a turtleneck, or a nice knit. I find that my tweed stitch J. Crew Rollneck Sweater is perfect for this look. Finish it off with a neutral slipper and a pair of scrunchy socks.

Crz Yoga SculptAir No Front Seam Leggings.

Opt for a pair of baggier jeans for this more casual outfit, which will be way comfier than a restrictive skinny or straight-leg jean. A looser pant also pairs better with a cozy boot, like this platform ankle boot. Finally, throw on a long-sleeve top or sweater with a cute vest for an outfit that feels very fall.

Vaoyiu Faux Suede Shearling Lined Vest.

Banana Republic The Icon Classic Wide-Leg Jean.

Project Cloud Ankle Platform Boots.

Industry observers note that okay, you caught me—I actually wore this outfit for Christmas last year instead of Thanksgiving, but it definitely works for either holiday! For this combo, start with your favorite skirt and a turtleneck top. Then top it off with a relaxed-fitting blazer (I love this houndstooth blazer, but any pattern or solid color will do). On the bottom, throw on a pair of tights and a knee-high boot.

Arach&Cloz Sleeveless Turtleneck Sweater.

Shannen Zitz is the Associate Style & Reviews Editor at Women's Health, where she covers all-things sneakers and activewear. Previously, she was an assistant editor at Prevention. Shannen graduated from the State University of New York at Cortland with a bachelor's degree in English. If she’s not reading or writing, you can probably find her frequenting the skincare and makeup forums on Reddit or hogging the squat rack at the gym.

XRP has spent a week unable to get back above $1. In November 2026, the token hit a two-year low of $0.895, and on Nov. 20, it was trading near $0.96. XRP is down 27.7% in November and about 51% since January, according to CryptoRank data.

The last time XRP lost more than 28% in a month was February 2025, when the token fell 29.3%. That month, the crypto market was also hit by a $1.5 billion hack of the Bybit exchange on Feb. 21.

In a recent development, XRP did not recover right away. From March to June 2025, the token gained about 4.5% in total, according to CryptoRank. In July 2025, XRP jumped 35%, and on July 18, 2025, it set its all-time high of $3.65. On the same day, U.S. President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act, the country's first stablecoin law. XRP is now 73% below that record.

In November 2021, XRP lost 10%, and it fell another 17% in December and 25.6% in January 2022. In November 2022, the month of the FTX collapse, the token dropped 11.8%, and it lost 16.9% in December. XRP finished 2022 down about 59% and gained 20.1% in January 2023.

According to CryptoRank, XRP's median return is -10.2% in November and -4.07% in December.

SoSoValue data reveals spot XRP ETFs have lost about $26 million to outflows since the start of November. About $19.1 million of that amount left the funds in the week ending Nov. 13.

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said on CNBC that investors had been selling crypto to buy shares in big listings. "People are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market, crypto included — Bitcoin, XRP — and moving it into SpaceX. The exact same thing happened coming into the Anthropic IPO. What we saw after the SpaceX IPO was a rally in the crypto markets. I think you'll see that happen here as well," he said.

Why TRUMP memecoin faces THESE risks ahead of Donald Trump’s exclusive dinner

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What exactly could keep investors from maintaining their conviction in TRUMP?
  • President Donald Trump is set to host an exclusive dinner for top holders of his TRUMP memecoin on Sunday.
  • According to recent reports, another problem to note is that 10 wallets make up 80.6% of the overall token supply.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What exactly could keep investors from maintaining their conviction in TRUMP?

For context, U.S. President Donald Trump is set to host an exclusive dinner for top holders of his TRUMP memecoin on Sunday. The timing is interesting. Politically, the Democrats’ victory in the midterm elections adds another layer of uncertainty for TRUMP holders. It could also increase scrutiny of Trump’s crypto-related ventures, making political developments an key factor to watch.

According to recent reports, another problem to note is that 10 wallets make up 80.6% of the overall token supply. So, while there are over 691k holders of TRUMP, a large percentage of these tokens are concentrated within a few wallets.

Against this backdrop, it’s no surprise that President Trump is hosting this dinner.

The logic is simple: If any large holders (there are 10 holders holding >80% of TRUMP) begin to sell TRUMP, it may cause panic selling. This risk is increased as TRUMP is already facing macroeconomic uncertainty.

So, is the dinner a “strategic” attempt to bring back interest in the memecoin?

The speculative capital in this cycle isn’t flowing into the memecoin market.

In a recent development, this marks a key difference from previous cycles, when investors often turned to memecoins during volatile market conditions to chase quick gains. But this time, the trend looks different. Despite broader market weakness, the memecoin market cap has continued to decline, with over $20 billion wiped out in Q4 so far.

But could President Trump’s dinner initiative change that? From a technical standpoint, TRUMP is deeply oversold, trading 99% below its all-time high and recently breaking below the key $1 level. If the dinner sparks fresh momentum, traders could look to take advantage of these lower price levels ahead of the event.

According to AMBCrypto, this could bring some speculative capital back into memecoins.

However, sustainability is a concern here. Traders often come in and out of memecoins, so there may be little sustainability in this position in the long-term. Furthermore, as 80% of Official Trump [TRUMP] supply is concentrated in only 10 wallets, traders may be cautious of building up spot exposure.

Alternatively, they could favor short-term speculative trades to capitalize on  any event-driven price action. This could lead to increased speculation. However, due to weak market conditions, it may cause a newly introduced wave of de-leveraging and put more pressure on the larger crypto market.

TRUMP’s supply concentration and political uncertainty could weaken investor confidence, increasing the risk of sudden sell-offs.

Trump’s dinner may revive short-term memecoin speculation, but weak market conditions could trigger fresh deleveraging.
